title: 1573-ski-turn-segmentation-causal-lstm
universal_lens: The primitive formalizes a strictly causal mapping from a finite history of noisy kinematic vectors to discrete biomechanical states. By enforcing temporal causality and utilizing physics-informed derivatives, it establishes a universal operator for real-time phase segmentation in non-stationary dynamical systems.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the per-frame binary outputs to a conformal prediction process over athlete movement quality. Bayesian uncertainty quantification is applied to the LSTM hidden states, generating calibrated risk intervals for ACL injury probability based on turn-segmentation confidence.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes this causal operator as the foundational state-transition engine for situational awareness. It segments continuous tracking telemetry into discrete tactical phases (e.g., acceleration bursts, cuts), enabling instantaneous workload accounting and dynamic fatigue modeling without future context leakage.

primitives.name: Strictly Causal IMU Segmentation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Can a smartphone IMU alone, processed strictly causally (no future context, deployable on-device), segment ski turns frame-by-frame in uncontrolled in-the-wild conditions well enough to serve as the foundation of a real-time injury-prevention assistant?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \hat{y}_t: predicted binary turn direction (dimensionless); f_\theta: causal neural operator; x_{1:t}: historical IMU vector sequence (m/s^2, rad/s).
primitives.assumptions: Calf-mounted device accurately proxies lower-limb kinematics; turn transitions are temporally brief; 10 Hz sampling suffices for relevant dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during extreme sensor noise, sub-10 Hz sampling rates, or highly erratic movements where the calf-to-limb kinematic isomorphism breaks down.

layer2.mapping: Directly isomorphic to GSE's `gse_causal_segment.py`. Replaces raw IMU with NGS tracking channels (x, y, speed) to detect live tactical phase shifts.
layer2.telemetry: Turn-level Intersection over Union (IoU) against ground-truth annotated segments.

primitives.name: Causal Biomechanical Feature Extractor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Physics-informed causal features: l2 magnitudes of accel/gyro, jerk (accel derivative), yaw 1st/2nd derivatives, local rolling stats; EMA filtering (causal); phase unwrapping of orientation; per-fold train-only normalization.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Jerk: rate of change of acceleration (m/s^3); Yaw derivatives: angular velocity/acceleration (rad/s, rad/s^2); EMA: Exponential Moving Average filter.
primitives.assumptions: Local rolling statistics and EMA filters introduce no look-ahead bias; physical derivatives remain stable under typical sensor noise floors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if sampling frequency drops below the Nyquist limit for the highest-order derivative (yaw 2nd derivative), causing numerical instability.

layer2.mapping: Adapted as the calibration 1x1 conv and multi-scale causal conv layer in GSE, extracting rotational inertia and acceleration bursts from player tracking data.
layer2.telemetry: Feature variance explained and sensitivity analysis on synthetic tracking perturbations.

primitives.name: Identity-Bias Free Validation Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Validation design Strict Leave-One-Subject-Out: for each skier with ≥5 descents, test on that skier's runs only, train from scratch on the rest (cold-start simulation); train/val split at run level (never window level) to avoid millisecond-adjacent leakage; all augmentation/preprocessing statistics from training folds only.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: LOSO: Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation fold; IoU: Intersection over Union metric (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Subjects exhibit distinct, non-overlapping kinematic signatures; temporal adjacency implies statistical dependence requiring strict partitioning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Protocol becomes computationally prohibitive or statistically weak if the number of subjects is extremely low (<3) or intra-subject variance exceeds inter-subject variance.

layer2.mapping: Establishes the mandatory audit standard for GSE injury models, preventing inflated performance metrics caused by randomized splits across correlated game events.
layer2.telemetry: Performance delta between LOSO and standard randomized k-fold validation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical contribution of the source text is the rigorous enforcement of temporal causality within a recurrent neural architecture to solve a biomechanical segmentation problem. The operator is defined as \hat{y}_t = f_\theta(x_{1:t}), ensuring that the prediction at time t relies exclusively on the past trajectory of inertial measurement unit (IMU) vectors. This formulation inherently rejects any reliance on future context, making it uniquely suited for real-time deployment on edge devices. The feature engineering pipeline further embeds physical priors—specifically, the computation of jerk (the first derivative of acceleration) and higher-order yaw derivatives—which act as high-frequency indicators of abrupt kinematic shifts characteristic of ski turns. These physics-informed features are filtered via an exponential moving average (EMA) to maintain strict causality while mitigating sensor noise. A critical dualism arises in the validation methodology. Standard machine learning practices often employ randomized k-fold cross-validation, which inadvertently introduces millisecond-adjacent data leakage when applied to continuous time-series. The authors circumvent this by implementing a strict Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) protocol combined with run-level splitting. This isolates the model's ability to generalize to entirely new kinematic signatures (cold-start scenarios), directly addressing the identity-bias phenomenon observed in wearable computing literature. The failure modes of this primitive are intrinsically tied to the breakdown of the underlying kinematic assumptions. If the calf-mounted smartphone fails to accurately proxy lower-limb dynamics—for instance, during extreme off-axis loading or equipment slippage—the feature space collapses. Furthermore, the assumption that a 10 Hz sampling rate captures the essential dynamics of a turn may fail for elite skiers executing micro-adjustments at significantly higher frequencies, leading to aliasing artifacts in the computed jerk and yaw derivatives.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to classical biomechanical gait analysis, which relied on laboratory-grade motion capture. The transition to wearable sensors necessitated robust signal processing, evolving from simple thresholding to Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). The adoption of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks marked a paradigm shift towards end-to-end learning of temporal dependencies. However, the explicit integration of physics-informed features and the rigorous LOSO validation protocol represent a recent maturation, responding to critiques of data leakage in sports analytics and wearable health monitoring.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the recreational skier, the system acts as an invisible, always-on safety net, translating complex kinematic risks into actionable feedback. The coach, conversely, views the segmented turns as a quantifiable metric of technique adherence, seeking to minimize high-risk maneuvers. The model itself operates as an opposing agent to human error, constantly predicting the onset of dangerous states based on historical patterns, effectively gamifying injury prevention through real-time state estimation.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists if the training data suffers from severe class imbalance, where safe turns overwhelmingly dominate high-risk maneuvers. In such regimes, the model may collapse to a trivial predictor of the majority class, yielding high accuracy but zero utility for injury prevention. Additionally, if the augmentation strategy (time warping) distorts the physical derivatives beyond physiological plausibility, it introduces synthetic noise that degrades the causal feature extractor's efficacy, mandating a strict bounds check on warping factors.
